panels.text: In 1854, a severe outbreak of cholera occurred near Broad Street in Soho, London. It killed 420 people.
The physician John Snow studied its causes. He was sceptical of the prevailing miasma theory, which held that disease came from something in the air.
Snow's hypothesis was that germ-contaminated water was the cause. He later used a dot map to illustrate how cases of cholera occurred around the Broad Street pump.
This discovery influenced public health and the construction of improved sanitation facilities beginning in the mid-19th century.
